name: Default Credentials
summary: Adversaries may leverage manufacturer or supplier set default credentials on control system devices. These default credentials may have administrative permissions and may be necessary for initial configuration of the device. It is general best practice to change the passwords for these accounts as soon as possible, but some manufacturers may have devices that have passwords or usernames that cannot be changed. analytics.name: Analytic 1888
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies successful authentication to an Industrial Control System (ICS) application such as a Human-Machine Interface (HMI), historian, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) server using credentials matching known default vendor passwords, from a logon source not associated with any authorized user. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. analytics.name: Analytic 2218
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies successful authentication to a field device using credentials matching documented vendor-default values, from a source not in the approved access list. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

analytics.name: Analytic 2255
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies successful Secure Shell (SSH) or application authentication using credentials matching known default vendor passwords on Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux assets. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.
